recipes.name: Quinoa with Chickpeas and Tomatoes
ingredients_raw: 1 pinch salt and pepper to taste

steps.text: Place the quinoa in a fine mesh strainer, and rinse under cold, running water until the water no longer foams. Bring the quinoa, salt, and water to a boil in a saucepan. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until the quinoa is tender, 20 to 25 minutes.
Once done, stir in the garbanzo beans, tomatoes, garlic, lime juice, and olive oil. Season with cumin, salt, and pepper. Sprinkle with chopped fresh parsley to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Quinoa with Chickpeas and Tomatoes
raw_recipe.description: This delicious recipe was presented to me by a vegan friend. The lime juice gives the quinoa a fresh flavor that can't be beat!

review.reviewBody: This one is a keeper, I substituted cilantro for the parsley and added avocados and red onions. Oh my, it even got better after sitting for a while.

I found a very similar recipe on another site and followed that one's suggestion of using 2 tablespoons fresh cilantro instead of the parsley. I used an entire can of garbanzo beans & more garlic. I also sauteed some chopped onion and wilted a head of spinach with a little more olive oil and tossed that with the mixture. Very flavorful mixture - especially after a day or two in the fridge.

This is one I'll definitely do again! I only combined the garbanzo beans with the quinoa in the last few minutes of cooking. I sautéed onions, garlic, green pepper, and mushrooms separately and added the seasonings to that veggie mixture before adding it onto the cooked quinoa with lime juice. On top of that, I added tomato, feta cheese, and avocado as a garnish and it was amazing!

Everyone liked this dish and I served it to a wide range of people at dinner. 

I used fresh coriander rather than parsley as I had none on hand.
I cooked the chickpeas and tomatoes in the quinoa for a bit to have the flavors meld.
I cooked the quinoa in vegetable broth not water
I used at least 3x the amount of cumin required and put in a pinch of red pepper. I kept tasting the dish saying it was tasteless and kept adding ground cumin until it registered.
I'll make it again, very popular at my house, but 1/2 tsp cumin is not enough!

Yum! I first sauteed a little bit of chopped onion and let that cook down a little. Then I added the quinoa and broth (instead of water) and it took more like 45 minutes to fully cook. Then I added a full can of chickpeas, about 1 cup of halved grape tomatoes (could have used more), and 2x the amount of dressing. I let it sit overnight to eat...easy and tasty!

Very enjoyable. I added chopped mushrooms, extra tomato and an avocado (excellent addition). You definitely need more water than it lists, so keep an eye on the quinoa (I had to add water a few times). I prepared it by adding the mushrooms and garlic 5 minutes or so before the quinoa would be finished, then a couple of minutes later adding the chickpeas and cumin, then adding the tomato. Then I would cook off the water (which the tomatoes would add to the dish). Once the extra water was cooked off I added the parsley. Add the avocado to your individual dish rather than the pot (because avocadoes don't store very well for leftovers). I also found the hoisin sauce perfected the dish.

I liked this recipe with some modifications. I used chicken stock instead of water. Used cherry tomatoes cut in half, substituted cilantro for the parsley and added the drained chickpeas in with the quinoa last ten minutes of cooking.

Excellent!

I would add much more chick peas...

Next day I made a frittata with leftovers adding an egg, cut up "pimientos de piquillo", lots of cilantro, a bit extra of salt and pepper. 
Using a pan, add a teaspoon of olive oil marinated with chili peppers, it gave it a delicious spicy flavor.
This is great. Made as written with these modifications: full can of garbanzos, 2 cloves garlic (which I sauteed with 1/2 cup red onions in a bit of olive oil), 1 1/2 tsp cumin.

OMG you must try this recipe! I promise you won't be disappointed. I chose this recipe because I needed to get rid of some quinoa in the pantry. I listened to previous reviews and replaced the tomato with spinach that I lightly wilted in a separate pan. I added about a 1/4 cup of diced red onion and another clove of garlic to the mix and replaced the parsley with cilantro. I also just threw in the entire can of chickpeas. HOLY COW! It was amazing to say the least. And so darn healthy. How can you say no to that?
This was so good!! I cooked the garlic in the quinoa with a little bit of chicken bouillon, and also added mushrooms. Will definitely make again!!
I enjoyed it but found the proportions a bit off. I doubled the amount of chickpeas, tomatoes and the olive oil/lime juice.
Definitely I’ll doing again, I used vegetable broth instead of water but next time I’ll use less liquid I cup of quinoa for two cup of liquid
Easy to follow recipe, albeit I didn't have all the ingredients. I wanted it more as a stew than a salad, so I added everything to the quinoa for the last 5 minutes of cook time.

This is one of my five recipes of all times and have been making it for years - at least since 2014 or so (even though it says it was updated in 2022?). I add half of a serrano pepper to give it just a smidge of a kick and a bit of kosher salt and it's perfect!
Delicious

I would make this again with some tweeks. It was good, it tastes nice at room temperature. It seems like it is supposed to be saladlike based on the way the recipe adds the last of the ingrediants. It will make a healthy lunch .
I dropped the tomato and used raisins and diced apples. Put in substantially more lime using juice, lime pulp and lime zest and shred lots of parsley. The kids will like it this way.
Oh so good!!! Added red onions, subbed cilantro for the parsely and added a little extra tomato!
The whole family LOVED it - and it was so easy to make.
